# CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#cosql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1204.pdf) · EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019 proceedings, printed pages 1962–1979

**Reading coverage:** All 18 PDF pages including sections 1–8, appendices A.1–A.3, dialogue examples and rendered interface/graph figures 4–11.

## Research question

Database conversations include context switches, ambiguity, unsupported questions and the need to explain returned results.

## Method

Crowd workers explore database tables while SQL-trained student experts execute queries, assign dialogue acts, clarify requests and describe results. Reference goals encourage connected exploration; subsequent review revises labels, queries and wording.

## Evaluation

The corpus separates databases across train/dev/test. Tasks are SQL-grounded dialogue-state tracking, description generation for successful SQL and user-dialogue-act prediction. Clarifications are supplied in tracking context after user affirmation; clarification quality itself is not evaluated.

## What the results support

Original baselines struggle with SQL interaction accuracy and distinguishing important acts despite high overall act accuracy. Template responses score worse on BLEU yet better on human logical correctness, showing that fluency metrics can miss semantic errors.

## Limits and qualifications

These are curated Wizard-of-Oz exchanges, not autonomous live-agent conversations. Users see database content and follow reference goals. INFER_SQL/CANNOT_ANSWER are operational annotation categories, not formal proofs of SQL inexpressibility. Historical baseline scores should not describe current models.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Foundational recorded interaction data, especially valuable when distinguishing supplied clarification context from active clarification-policy evaluation.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
